Subject: Vector relevance discovery — index scale & SLA next steps

Hi Elena / Daniel,

Thanks again for the call today — appreciated the context. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Pain points you highlighted
- Search relevancy dropping for product pages after the reindex last quarter (CTR down ~8%).
- Slow re-ranking on 95th percentile tail (observed ~450ms for srv-side rerank when loaded).
- Cost pressure: want per-query inference under $0.003 at current 18M queries/month volume.

Current stack you mentioned
- Vector DB: Milvus (self-hosted) for primary index; Postgres for metadata.
- Ingestion: nightly batches (~500k vectors/day) + sporadic realtime upserts from user events (2-5k/day).
- Model: off-the-shelf sentence-transformers for embeddings; separate BERT-based reranker used for re-ranking.

Success criteria for pilot
1) Match or improve top-10 relevance (human eval + CTR)
2) 95th p99 rerank latency < 200ms (end-to-end for rerank stage)
3) Cost target: sub-$0.003/query at 18M/mo (including embeddings lookups + rerank)
4) Simple integration (SDK + 1-2 infra changes) and SOC2 evidence for procurement.

What Redwood proposes (high level)
- Hybrid approach: host embeddings in your Milvus cluster + Redwood-hosted rerank instances with adaptive batching and prefix caching.
- Autoscaling policy that keeps p95 under 150ms while batching small queries to save unit cost.
- Pilot: 4-week technical validation, ingest 5% sample of prod index (~900k vectors), run A/B on 10% traffic.

Attachments I’m sharing: redwood-embeddings-playbook.pdf (short handbook), sample cost estimate template.

Immediate next steps
- Can we schedule a 60-min deep-dive with your infra lead + one engineer this week? I’m available Thu 8/12 10:00-12:00 PT or Fri 8/13 14:00-16:00 PT.
- Rishi will prepare an initial architecture sketch and cost estimate once you confirm index size and expected QPS distribution.

If anything above is off, please flag and I’ll update. Thanks — looking forward to the deep dive.

Best,
Connor O
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0198

Subject: Re: Vector relevance discovery — index scale & SLA next steps

Connor,

Thanks for the clear summary — this looks right to us. A few clarifications and extra numbers: 

- Index scale: ~120M active vectors (product catalog + embeddings for variants). Cold archival layer ~20M older items.
- QPS profile: peak 1.2k qps (90th ~900 qps) with very spiky traffic during daytime windows. Average monthly queries ~18M as you noted.
- Batch patterns: nightly full batch ~500k inserts, nightly compaction. We also have near-real-time upserts ~3k/day.
- Current rerank: separate service doing a BERT rerank for top-50 candidates; that service sits on 4xV100s and is costly — we’d like to reduce the footprint while improving tail.

Questions for Redwood: 
1) Does Redwood support prefix/KV cache that persists across requests to avoid recomputing early layers? We’re concerned about memory pressure with a 120M index.
2) For the pilot, can you provide an architecture diagram showing where Milvus sits vs. Redwood hosted components?
3) Compliance: can you share what SOC2 evidence we can expect in the pilot (logs, tenant isolation notes)? Procurement will need this before we spin up a dedicated test.

We can do the deep-dive on Thu 8/12 at 10:30 PT (Connor, are you able to do 10:30?). Attendees: me (Product), Daniel (Infra), Priya Shah (Security, priya.shah@shopwave.com), and Ahmed (search eng).

I attached a small sample of query latency histograms from our prod window (shopwave-sample-qps.csv) to illustrate spikes.

Thanks,
Elena
Head of Product | ShopWave, Inc.
elena@shopwave.com

Subject: Re: Vector relevance discovery — index scale & SLA next steps

Elena, excellent — thanks for the numbers and the histogram. A few quick answers and what we’ll bring to the deep-dive: 

1) Prefix / KV cache: yes — Redwood supports persistent KV caching for hot prefixes and can layer an LRU cache in front of Milvus lookups. That reduces repeated transformer work for frequently queried prefixes. For a 120M corpus we recommend a 2-4M warm cache window depending on query skew.

2) Architecture doc: attached is a concise sketch (also dropping into the Drive link). High level: 
- Milvus remains your vector store (we support direct Milvus connectors).
- Redwood-hosted rerank pool sits in front of the BERT reranker with a light-weight re-ranking shim that handles adaptive batching and fallback rules.
- Optional: Redwood-managed embedding store (if you prefer offloading vector storage) — we can pilot either way.

3) SOC2/compliance: for pilots we provide audit logs, tenant isolation notes, and an SOC2 summary. For Private/Dedicated pilots we can surface more detailed evidence; procurement typically wants the SOC2 report + runbook for data retention. Priya will be able to review the docs in the deep-dive.

What we’ll bring to the deep-dive (Thu 8/12 10:30 PT)
- Rishi: cost + perf tradeoff scenarios (quantized models, batching profiles)
- Marissa: integration checklist + sample rollout plan (A/B -> canary rollout -> full)
- Connor: program/contract and pilot success metrics alignment

I’ve attached a preliminary cost estimate (redwood-cost-estimate-embeddings.xlsx) that assumes you host Milvus and Redwood runs rerank. We’ll refine after the call.

See you Thu 10:30 PT. Calendar invite to follow.

Best,
Connor
